findings.where: front matter 'progress | block | narrative partial at a milestone, else the one-line Where/Next status (shiploop_narrative) | 900 | refuse'
findings.evidence: Nothing bounds the narrative where it is produced (shiploop_narrative.py has no limit; narrative_facts lists up to 3 achieved items with 100-character headlines and up to 3 upcoming titles). Live outer-stage narratives reach 947-1,111. A calibrated synthetic step-plan narrative is 943 at W2 of 4, 1,045 at W3 of 4 and 1,327 at W4 of 7. W2's step-plan follows W1's carry-forward, a group end, so it is a milestone (navigator milestone: last['stage'] in _GROUP_ENDS). tmpl.render raises on a 953-character value. So in any run with four or more items, the step-plan packet (and implement's, which declares the same slot) never prints. This is the class round 2 fixed for the revisit blocks (a refuse slot nothing upstream bounds). tmpl.validate checks 'producer bound' only for include slots, so it did not catch this. Not run on a multi-item engine state.
findings.fix: Slot source: 'the narrative partial at a milestone when it is at most 900 characters, else the one-line Where/Next status (navigator status block)'. The fallback is short and bounded. Make tmpl.validate require a producer bound or a computed bound for every refuse-class slot, not only includes. Add a test that renders narrative_facts at the structural maxima.

findings.where: front matter 'keepalive_marker | scalar | "SHIPLOOP-RUN run=<run_id> rev=<revision> dir=<RUN>" | run+65 | refuse'
findings.evidence: The marker is run+63+digits(revision), so run+65 fits only revisions up to 99. tmpl.render at revision 100 raises 'value of 162 characters over its bound 161'. One item took about 32 revisions in the Battleship run, and that 1-item run ended at revision 50, so a 3-4 item run passes 100 inside its later items. From then on every packet of both templates fails to render (implement declares the same bound). The keepalive hook's MARKER regex reads rev=(?P<rev>\d+), so it accepts any length.
findings.fix: keepalive_marker bound: run+69 (6 revision digits, matching the revision slot's bound 6). Better, derive the bound of every install- and state-built scalar from its formula's parts.

A new plan with new IDs breaks test-spec's case IDs, which costs another send-back. prep_values' locator for the block is 'the revise result', not a path.
findings.fix: Split the slot into revisit_locators (refuse, 250: 'Amend: RUN/results/<previous step-plan>.md · Sent back by <stage>: RUN/results/<send-back>.md · <headline>') and revisit_summary (excerpt, 650, shrinkable). decision_20.what_it_kept: A fresh model still knows what 'done' means. 'Done when' points at the loop's Exit, and the packet says to start the loop before any work. The runtime's start packet prints work, conditions.exit and conditions.repeat (verified in round 2, and E5 is in requires). Methods 4-7 and the form state the formats and most gate rules. Every gate anchor still prints. The callback stays the third line after the header, and the keepalive line is unchanged. A refusal for a loop that never started names the start command (check_loop_packet 'has not run ... Start it with').
decision_20.what_it_moved_out: Four rules: 'Never stop cancelled' (SP3-6), exit 3's 'every criterion is satisfied by a step' and 'unless the whole item is tests' (SP2-12), and the step-plan Repeat's blocked rule (SP3-8). The model sees them only after starting the loop. None stalls a run, and --check-only names the step rules. They went unnoticed because none of them has a gates row (SP2-11).
decision_20.contradictions: Method 4's 'Tests are not a step' is stricter than the gate's test-only exception, and RULES' blocked rule differs from the loop Repeat's.

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes most of round 2. SP2-1's P0 is gone (the revisit block is excerpt-class with the summary at 600). Fixed: the stop outcomes, the restart guard, the KNOWLEDGE locators, the look-back label, E1 in requires, and the card's ## Testing printing whole. Decision 20 broke no route. 'Done' is still defined by the Method, the form and the loop's own Exit, which the runtime prints at start. It moved four rules into the loop's print only, and the gates table, missing those rows, could not notice. The template is not ready to land once requires are met. Two refuse-class slots that nothing bounds would stall real runs: the progress narrative at 900 (943 at W2 of a 4-item run, 1,327 at W4 of 7) and the keepalive marker at run+65, which fails from revision 100 (both verified in the renderer). The budget's static guarantee relies on shrinking the revisit block to a single-locator pointer, which loses the plan the model must amend. The command bounds assume unquoted paths. Also, the reviewed print was rendered with allow_over_budget true; with the budget enforced, a renderer bug turns the card section and ## Commands into pointers after any shrink. Each of these is a bound or slot-class fix of a few lines. None needs a new feature.
top_changes: Bound every refuse-class slot where it is produced, or compute its bound. progress falls back to the one-line status above 900. The keepalive marker gets run+69. cmd and path slots take the built value's length, so quoting cannot overflow them. Make tmpl.validate refuse a refuse-class slot of any kind without a producer or computed bound (SP3-1, SP3-2, SP3-4, SP3-10).

Make the budget rule protect the send-back. Split revisit_block into refuse-class locators (250) plus a shrinkable summary, list the previous step-plan result in source_results, shrink pooled slots first, and re-render from the initial pool. Render the examples with the budget enforced (SP3-3, SP3-5, SP3-7, SP2-10).

Put back in the packet what decision 20 moved out, and pay for it with duplicates. Method 4 gets 'every criterion is in some step's' and the test-only exception. The Done-report line becomes 'never cancelled; a user's stop is the pause command'. Add gates rows for the step-sizing, cancelled-loop and read-only-check refusals, so the anchor check guards them. Drop the Done-when parenthetical and the SP-26 clause, and name `owner_stage` in Method 8 (SP2-12, SP3-6, SP2-11, SP3-11, SP2-8).
